era.title: After the Soviet Union
era.summary: The Soviet Union and Yugoslavia have broken into new states, Czechoslovakia has split in two and Eritrea has just won independence.

events.title: Kuwait is liberated
events.detail: A US-led coalition drove Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in February 1991, ending a seven-month occupation and Iraq's claimed annexation.

events.title: The Baltic states break free
events.detail: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania restored the independence they had lost in 1940. Moscow recognised them in September 1991.

events.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
events.detail: On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union was dissolved, leaving its twelve remaining republics, from Ukraine to Kazakhstan, as independent states.

events.title: Yugoslavia breaks apart
events.detail: Slovenia, Croatia and Macedonia declared independence in 1991, and Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992. War followed in Croatia and Bosnia.

events.title: A smaller Yugoslavia
events.detail: Serbia and Montenegro formed the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in April 1992, with a new tricolour flag.

events.title: Mujahideen take Kabul
events.detail: The communist government fell in April 1992 and an Islamic State of Afghanistan was proclaimed. Rival factions soon fought over the capital.

events.title: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully
events.detail: On 1 January 1993 Czechoslovakia divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, without a shot fired.

events.title: Eritrea becomes independent
events.detail: After thirty years of war and a referendum, Eritrea became independent on 24 May 1993. Ethiopia lost its whole coastline.

notes: Snapshot taken around June 1993, after Eritrea's independence (24 May 1993).

Cambodia: shown with the UNTAC-period Supreme National Council flag. Sources differ on whether the 1948 flag was readopted in June or on 24 September 1993; if mid-1993 is read as July or later, KH could be left unassigned.

Bosnia and Herzegovina is drawn whole, though in mid-1993 Bosnian Serb forces held roughly 70% of it and Croat forces much of the rest. Likewise Croatia is drawn whole despite the Serb-held Krajina, Georgia includes Abkhazia (war ongoing), Azerbaijan includes Nagorno-Karabakh, Moldova includes Transnistria.
Kosovo and Vojvodina are given labels within FRY as Serbia's autonomous provinces (Kosovo's autonomy had been revoked in 1989-90 and an unrecognised Republic of Kosova ran a parallel administration).
FRY uses the spec's canonical id; the 2011 fragment uses SCG for the identical flag (Serbia and Montenegro, 2003-06). Reconcile if desired.

Saint Martin and Saint Barthelemy were communes of Guadeloupe until 2007, so they join FR-971 as FR|Guadeloupe. New Caledonia flew only the French tricolour in 1993. Tokelau used the New Zealand flag until 2009.

Palau (PW) was the last part of the UN Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands under US administration until October 1994; shown as US_TTPI|Palau, as in the 1990 era (it already flew its own 1981 flag locally).
East Timor and the Palestinian territories are contested polities (hatched) under the occupying states' flags and colours. Oslo I came in September 1993, after this snapshot.
South Sudan is joined to Sudan without a label; the 1972 Southern Region had been abolished in 1983 and civil war was ongoing.

Somaliland (SO~somaliland) left as Somalia (de facto independent since 1991, unrecognised), as in other eras. Western Sahara, Northern Cyprus and Taiwan left as their modern selves, matching their 1993 situation.
Walvis Bay (inside the NA unit) remained South African until March 1994; not representable.

Minor shade-only differences not assigned: Japan (pre-1999 Hinomaru), Paraguay, Ecuador, Guatemala, Nicaragua arms tweaks. Honduras' 1949 flag is current again in 2026 per Commons, so left unassigned.

Event-only polities USSR, YUGOSLAVIA, CZECHOSLOVAKIA, AF_1987 and the asset-flag modern ids (EE, LV, UA, KZ, SI, HR, SK) are defined so chips resolve; SD, FR, NZ are defined explicitly as parents of other units and match the implicit modern polities.
Eritrea is assigned ER_1993: its first flag (24 May 1993 to 5 Dec 1995) differed from today's in proportions and emblem.
Netherlands Antilles uses AN_1986 (5-star flag, as in the 1990 era); NL_ANTILLES is the 1976 era's id for the 1959-86 6-star flag.

Inside other units and not representable: South Africa's four nominally independent homelands (Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Venda, Ciskei) until April 1994; de facto Chechen Republic of Ichkeria; Armenian-held Nagorno-Karabakh and surrounding districts (Kelbajar April 1993).

Metropoles UK (with England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland) and Portugal join GB_EMPIRE / PT_EMPIRE with their own labels, as in the 1990 era, since Hong Kong and Macau are still colonies. Names 'British Empire'/'Portuguese Empire' read anachronistically for 1993.

Other British dependent territories (Bermuda, Cayman, Turks and Caicos, Montserrat, BVI, Anguilla, Falklands, BIOT) keep their own polities with the pre-1999 flags; South Georgia (GS_1992) flew its first Blue Ensign of 1992-99 (arms granted Feb 1992). Gibraltar, Saint Helena and Pitcairn flags were already today's. The 1990 era leaves most of these implicit, so they change flag 1990->1993->2011.
Kuwait (KW_OCCUPIED in 1990) is free again: Iraqi forces expelled 26-28 Feb 1991. KW and KW_OCCUPIED are defined here only for the event chips.

Ids aligned with the 1990/1949/1960 fragments: RW_1962, MM_1989, WS_1962, PH_1936. ZA_1928 uses the 1982-94 bright-blue file (matches 2011); 1939/1990 use the dark file under the same id and 1976 the redirect to it, so the merger must pick one per id.
Moldova's 1990-2010 flag (slightly different arms) is not assigned, as a minor variant.
